correctness.rationale: For right multiplication by g^b the basis action on C_m is the affine bijection R_b(x)=tx+(1-t)b. An invariant subspace is invariant under its inverse by finite dimensionality, so it is invariant under R_b R_c^(-1), which translates by (1-t)(b-c). This covers every cyclic displacement. For left multiplications the corresponding difference translates by t(a-c), again covering the regular cyclic action. In either direction closure is therefore equivalent to an ordinary group-ring ideal: the converse holds because every ordinary ideal is a power of (g-1) and is preserved by the two multiplier automorphisms. Over any field of characteristic p, g^(p^s)-1=(g-1)^(p^s), and the ideals of K[z]/(z^m) are exactly (z^a): a nonzero element of least z-adic order a is z^a times a unit. The basis transport multiplies the two automorphic images in this ordinary ring; it gives the stated span even for zero powers and saturated exponents. Induction on the product tree gives J^k for any parenthesization, nonzero for k=m-1 and zero for k=m.
residual_risks: Exact finite checks recorded for orders 3, 5 and 9 are illustrative only. The proof uses both Latin units and the defining-characteristic prime-power cyclic group algebra.

originality.rationale: No checked source was found to print precisely this modular left-and-right classification verbatim. Nevertheless it is a direct consequence of the prior Alexander transport and the standard ordinary cyclic regular-module chain. From the published transport one has I*1=alpha(I) for any right ideal and 1*I=beta(I) for any left ideal. Invertibility gives equality, and surjectivity of the other multiplier then gives closure under ordinary multiplication by every element. Conversely all ordinary ideals of the truncated polynomial ring are multiplier-invariant. This mechanically yields the asserted exhaustion in both directions. It is also immediate from the published permutation-module description for the right side, since a quotient of two affine translations gives every cyclic shift, with the same calculation for the left side. The powers and independence of parenthesization are already covered by the prior general augmentation theorem; the pairwise product formula is ordinary multiplication of preserved powers. The failure is deductive prior coverage, not evidence of a verbatim duplicate or reliance on inaccessible literature.
residual_risks: No exhaustive priority statement about an explicit earlier wording is made. The decision rests on the immediate mathematical implication, independent of whether the formulation appears elsewhere.
